description: Fig. 8 is a two-panel TEM composite of Fe-(26-28)Mn-(11-12)Al-(0.9-1.15)C (wt.%) triplex steel deformed at room temperature by tensile test, illustrating the SIP (shear-induced plasticity) effect. (a) is a TEM bright-field image with a 2 µm scale bar: a broad, dark, dislocation-dense shear band cuts diagonally across the field (upper-left to lower-right) and a second dark band approaches from the lower right; between them the austenite matrix appears bright with fine internal striations and thinner dark slip traces aligned parallel to the main band, i.e. shear bands on {111} planes in austenite. (b) is a TEM dark-field image with a 500 nm scale bar recorded using the superlattice reflection (210) of the ⟨001⟩ fcc zone axis; it shows a very regular, grid-like (near-checkerboard) array of fine bright precipitates — κ-carbides, 20–30 nm in size, coherent with the austenitic matrix — uniformly distributed over the whole field. Together the two panels make the figure's argument: a homogeneous dispersion of coherent nanosized κ-carbides produces uniformly arranged shear bands on {111} planes, the microstructural basis of the SIP effect. No axis scales or numeric labels other than the two scale bars are printed; particle size (20–30 nm) is stated only in the caption.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field image of deformed triplex steel with a 2 µm scale bar; a thick dark shear band runs diagonally across the field with parallel thinner slip/shear traces in the bright austenite matrix and dark dislocation-dense regions at the lower right.

TEM dark-field image (scale bar 500 nm) taken with the (210) superlattice reflection of the ⟨001⟩ fcc zone axis, showing a dense, regular grid-like arrangement of fine bright κ-carbide particles in the austenitic matrix.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field image with a printed scale bar of 2 µm.
Panel (a) shows broad dark shear bands running diagonally through a brighter austenite matrix, with thinner parallel dark traces between the main bands.
Panel (b) is a TEM dark-field image with a printed scale bar of 500 nm.
Panel (b) shows a dense, regular grid-like (cross-hatched) arrangement of fine bright particles distributed uniformly across the whole field.
The caption identifies (a) as a TEM bright-field image exhibiting shear bands on {111} planes in austenite.

The caption identifies (b) as a TEM dark-field image showing the regular arrangement of κ-carbides of 20–30 nm size coherent to the austenitic matrix (printed in the caption as 'j-carbides', an encoding artefact for κ-carbides).
The caption states the dark-field image was taken using the superlattice reflection (210) of the ⟨001⟩ fcc zone axis (printed as 'h001i fcc zone axis').
The figure concerns Fe-(26-28)Mn-(11-12)Al-(0.9-1.15)C (wt.%) triplex steels deformed at room temperature by tensile test.
The citing text states that a regular distribution of nanosized κ-carbides coherent in the austenite matrix gives rise to uniformly arranged shear bands on {111} planes, as shown in Fig. 8.
Neither panel prints an axis scale, magnification figure, or numeric data label; the only printed quantities are the two scale bars (2 µm and 500 nm).
The particle size range 20–30 nm for the κ-carbides is not measurable from the pixels of (b); it is asserted only in the caption.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the exact number and spacing of individual shear bands cannot be counted reliably due to overlapping contrast
caption typography: 'j-carbides' and 'h001i fcc zone axis' are encoding artefacts (κ-carbides and ⟨001⟩), not literal chemical/symbol labels
